text:
maria: Quick note — QA found shared saved-query links don't always reproduce route/model context.
kevin: Steps to reproduce?
maria: Save query on route `orders` with model `gpt-4-redwood`. Share link. If you open link while on route `billing`, the Console opens the saved query payload but keeps route `billing` selected. Filters apply to billing -> confusing results.
sasha: That matches current design: saved queries store only the query blob (filters, time range), not UI scope. Keeps DB small.
ben: Users expect a link to reproduce an exact view. We need to pick behavior: "link reproduces full view" vs "link applies query to current scope".
maria: For debugging and regressions we need deterministic reproduction including route/model/time. Prefer persisted anchor.
kevin: Two options:
  - Quick experiment: support deep-link params e.g. `?saved=ID&anchor=route:orders&model:gpt-4-redwood&time=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z` and show a banner asking user to apply anchor.
  - Long-term: extend saved_query object with optional scope fields (route_id, model_slug, time_range, scope_enum).
sasha: Param approach is fastest (front-end only) but brittle: copy-pasted links may lose anchor. Backend schema is cleaner.
ben: Also surface routing and quota hints when anchor refers to a dedicated model: show if current user has access or will be routed to hosted fallback.
maria: UX suggestion: don't auto-swap routes. Show a non-modal banner: "This saved view was anchored to route=orders, model=gpt-4-redwood. [Apply anchor]  [Use my current route]" with small copy about routing/permissions.
kevin: Backend constraints: GET /api/saved_queries/:id currently returns `{query_blob}`. Adding scope fields requires DB migration and touching several consumers. We can add deprecating fields later.
sasha: Plan: implement anchor query-param + banner (front-end) this sprint as an experiment. If adoption is good, proceed with backend schema in next cycle.
ben: Telemetry: emit `analytics.saved_query.open` with tags `{saved_id, anchor_present, anchor_applied, opener, current_route, anchor_route, model_in_anchor}`. Also record `routing_decision` if fallback used.
maria: Also need audit trail: if a saved query is migrated to include scope, track `migrated_from` and migration date.
kevin: Add `scope` enum to saved queries: `global`, `route_scoped`, `org_scoped`. Affects permission checks and default anchor behavior.
sasha: I'll mock banner copy and visuals and post in #product-design. I'll PR front-end changes and wire telemetry event.
ben: I'll write the telemetry event schema and add validation to the ingestion pipeline.
maria: Created ticket CONSOLE-842 in the tracker: "Saved-query deep-link anchoring + banner + telemetry". Assignees: sasha, kevin, ben, maria. Due 2026-03-20.
console-bot: Ticket CONSOLE-842 created by maria: "Saved-query deep-link anchoring + banner + telemetry" — assignees: sasha, kevin, ben, maria — due 2026-03-20.
kevin: Also we should consider sampling/timezone normalization in anchor time ranges — avoid ambiguous ISO strings without timezone.
maria: Good catch. Normalize to UTC and show local fallback copy.
ben: I'll add `anchor_time_tz` to telemetry and require ISO8601 with `Z`.
sasha: Will include sample link examples in PR and e2e regression tests.
maria: Thanks — adding follow-up task to CONSOLE-842: backfill top 500 popular saved queries with scope fields after migration is ready.
kevin: Sounds good. Ping when the banner PR is ready for review.
sasha: Will do.
